issue_context.title: String.IsInterned always interns the string passed in to it
comments: Thank you for reporting this issue!

Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/area-system-runtime See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
### Description Through .NET 8.0, `System.String.IsInterned(System.String)` returned either the same string passed in to it (if that string was interned) or `null` (if the string was not interned). This matches the [documentation for this method](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.string.isinterned?view=net-8.0). The implementation for .NET 8.0 is: ``` public static string? IsInterned(string str) { ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(str, "str"); return str.IsInterned(); } ``` As of .NET 9.0 Preview 1, `IsInterned` now always interns the string passed in to it. Its implementation is: ``` public static string? IsInterned(string str) { ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(str, "str"); Intern(new StringHandleOnStack(ref str)); return str; } ``` This appears to be an unintentional change in behavior while converting FCalls to QCalls in #95670. ### Reproduction Steps When run under .NET Framework or versions of .NET [Core] up to 8.0, this snippet indicates that the string is not interned (as expected). When run under .NET 9.0 Preview 1, this snippet indicates that the string _is_ interned (because it just interned it). ``` string value = Guid.NewGuid().ToString(); Console.WriteLine($"Interned == {ReferenceEquals(value, string.IsInterned(value))}"); ``` [StringInterningRepro.zip](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/files/14517340/StringInterningRepro.zip) ### Expected behavior I do not expect `System.String.IsInterned` to intern the string passed in to it. ### Actual behavior `System.String.IsInterned` interns the string passed in to it. ### Regression? This behavior is new with .NET 9.0 Preview 1. It was not seen with .NET Framework or any prior .NET [Core] versions. ### Known Workarounds _No response_ ### Configuration - .NET 9.0 Preview 1 - Windows 11 - x64 ### Other information _No response_
